topic: How much water a household really needs for 72 hours

content.hook: How much water does your household really need?

slides.title: How much *water* do you really need?
slides.body: A calm 72-hour calculation for your household.

slides.title: The simple rule: *3 litres*
slides.body: Plan about 3 litres per person per day for drinking and basic food preparation.

slides.title: Now multiply it out
slides.body: 3 litres × 3 days = 9 litres per person. A family of four needs about 36 litres.

slides.title: Some people need *more*
slides.body: Young children, older people, anyone unwell, hot weather and pets. Add a comfortable margin.

slides.title: Hygiene is *extra*
slides.body: Washing hands and brushing teeth need water too. Store some extra if you have the space.

slides.title: Short on space? Spread it out
slides.body: Water is heavy. Use bottles under beds, in wardrobes and low cupboards instead of one big pile.

slides.title: Date it. Check it. *Rotate* it.
slides.body: Write the date on each bottle. Check twice a year and swap in fresh water.

content.caption:
Water is the first thing to sort for a 72-hour plan. And the maths is easier than it looks.

A common rule of thumb in official guidance: about 3 litres per person, per day. That covers drinking and basic food preparation.

3 litres × 3 days = 9 litres per person.
Family of four? About 36 litres.

A few calm tweaks:
• Young children, older people, anyone unwell, hot weather and pets can mean more. Add a margin.
• Washing and brushing teeth are extra. Store a bit more if you can.
• Water is heavy. Spread bottles around your home instead of one big stack.
• Write the date on each bottle and check twice a year.

That's it. No panic, no bunker. Just a few bottles and a plan.

Ready72h is a household planner for the first 72 hours of a crisis. It's based on guidance from Sweden's MSB, Germany's BBK and Poland's RCB, and includes a full supply checklist with a water section.
